 Sports cars, minivans and SUVs recalled in Canada over potentially detaching wheels, fuel leak risk and other safety defects
 Land Rover, Porsche, Toyota and Volvo vehicle recalls were reported by Transport Canada between Oct. 16 and 23.
 By Metroland Staff Insidehaltoncom

 A few car brands issued vehicle recalls that affect sports cars, minivans and SUVs in Canada.
 See below for the vehicle recalls that were reported by Transport Canada during the week of Oct. 19 to 23.
 Porsche
 ARTICLE CONTINUES BELOW 
 Porsche issued a recall that affects several vehicle models.
 Affected cars include:
 ARTICLE CONTINUES BELOW 
 2024 Porsche 718 Spyder
 2024 Porsche Cayman GT4
 2024 Porsche 911 Carrera
 2024 Porsche 911 GT3
 2024 Porsche 911 Turbo
 The recall impacts 111 cars in Canada.
 ARTICLE CONTINUES BELOW 
 This recall is an expansion of Transport Canada recall No. 2024-646. It only affects vehicles equipped with optional central locking wheels.
 ARTICLE CONTINUES BELOW
 The centre wheel lock(s) may not have been manufactured properly on some vehicles, and they could break and cause the wheel(s) to separate from the vehicle.
 “A wheel separation could cause a loss of control and increase the risk of a crash. Additionally, a wheel that separates could create a hazard for others,” the recall, last updated Oct. 20, said.
 To reduce the safety risk, Porsche advises owners not to drive their vehicle until the recall repairs are completed.
 Porsche will notify owners by mail and advise them to contact a dealer to arrange to have the vehicle towed to the dealership. The centre wheel locks will be inspected and, if necessary, replaced.
 Land Rover
 Land Rover issued a recall on the 2022 to 2026 Range Rover.
 ARTICLE CONTINUES BELOW 
 More than 7,000 SUVs are affected.
 Water could leak into the rear-view camera and cause the rear-view camera image not to display properly or at all on some vehicles.
 “A rear-view camera image that doesn’t display properly could reduce a driver’s ability to see behind the vehicle while backing up. This could increase the risk of a crash,” the recall, last updated Oct. 20, said.
 Land Rover will notify owners by mail and advise them to take their vehicle to a dealership to inspect and, if necessary, replace the rear-view camera. Additionally, the dealer will add drainage holes to the tailgate trim.
 Toyota
 Toyota issued a pair of recalls recently.
 Land Cruiser
 ARTICLE CONTINUES BELOW 
 Toyota’s first recall is on the 2024 to 2027 Land Cruiser.
 It affects nearly 7,000 SUVs.
 The plastic fuel tube on the top of the fuel tank could disconnect from the main metal fuel tube on some vehicles, which could result in fuel leaking and causing the engine to stall.
 “A fuel leak can create the risk of a fire,” the recall, last updated Oct. 19, said.
 Toyota will notify owners by mail and advise them to take their vehicle to a dealership to inspect the fuel tube connection. The dealer will install a clamp at the connection and, if necessary, replace the plastic fuel tube.
 Sienna Hybrid
 Toyota’s second recall is on the 2022 to 2026 Sienna Hybrid. It affects more than 24,000 minivans.
 ARTICLE CONTINUES BELOW 
 The mechanisms that lock the second-row seat recliners in position may disengage when a seatbelt pretensioner activates under certain conditions. This could cause the seatback(s) to move in a crash. More details are available at the accompanying link.
 News 
 Toyota Sienna recall asks 24K Canadian minivan owners not to use the middle-row seats 
 Metroland Staff 
 Volvo
 Volvo issued a recall on the 2025 and 2026 model years of the EX30 and EX30 Cross Country.
 It affects more than 2,000 electric SUVs.
 The cushions within the front seat headrests may not have been attached properly, which could cause the cushion(s) to move or detach in a crash.
 “A head restraint cushion that moves or detaches in a crash could increase the risk of an injury,” the recall, last updated Oct. 16, said.
 ARTICLE CONTINUES BELOW 
 Volvo will notify owners by mail and advise them to take their vehicle to a dealership to repair the front seat head restraint cushions.
